statements.quote: Personalization is measured by comparing every AI response to the individual’s profile to assess whether the response contains either explicit or implicit cues (see Supplementary Materials for additional detail).

Our results are robust to LLM judgments using different AI models (e.g., GPT4o-mini vs. Gemini), evaluation prompts (e.g., absolute vs. relative assessment), and judgements correlate highly with human expert ratings (see Supplementary Materials).

These findings are robust to the choice of evaluator: the significant effect of personalization persists when campaigns are scored by an ensemble of 7 alternative LLMs—including both smaller, efficient models (β = 0.35, p = 0.03) and larger, frontier models (β = 0.36, p = 0.05)—and when applying a qualitatively different evaluation framework (β = 0.50, p = 0.008) (see Supplementary Materials, Fig. S1,Table S4).

statements.quote: While turn-level analysis highlights what functional changes occur in personalized conversations, a distributional analysis of response embeddings reveals when and how these distinctive patterns emerge (see Supplementary Materials Methods for additional details).

Checked anonymously with Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 on 2026-10-09. The PDF p. 28 link and both URLs in forms/c401.json data_and_code are the same deposit. Landing page HTTP 200; node metadata HTTP 200, public=true, current_user_permissions=['read']. All 32 recursive OSF file-list requests returned HTTP 200; pagination and all subfolders were traversed. Exactly 126 files, excluding folders. The 50 files listed here prioritize data, documentation, and relevant code. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/kzuge/children/ returned HTTP 200 with zero children. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/kzuge/files/ returned HTTP 200 with osfstorage as the only provider.

The README identifies this as code and de-identified data for the exact paper title. Main data download https://osf.io/download/69989893fb11d89d0d505920/ returned HTTP 200 and 781538 bytes. creativity_df_CI.csv has 331 rows, 202 columns, and 331 distinct, nonempty participant_id values. Directly observed randomization counts: basegpt=116 (Generic AI), creativegpt=114 (Personalized AI), creativegpt_rand=101 (Partially personalized AI). campaign_quality_score, campaign_wc, total_campaign_components, and marketing_terms_wc are numeric and nonmissing for every participant in each arm; these cover S1-O1, S1-O4, S1-O5, and S1-O6. Use randomization, not the codebook's numeric treatment labels: observed treatment_numeric is -1 for basegpt, 1 for creativegpt, and 0 for creativegpt_rand, whereas the codebook incorrectly describes 0/1/2.

LLM Elo file elo_ratings_gpt-4o-mini.csv contains 331 rows and the columns participant_id, randomization, run_1, run_2, run_3, run_4, run_5. All five run scores are nonmissing in all arms. Its ID set and arm assignments exactly match the main dataset. Per-person averaging across the five runs is possible before computing arm summaries. plot_elo_ratings.R lines 19-20 still select columns 4:8 although the public file has only seven columns; analysis must use the named run_1 through run_5 fields and join by participant_id. The supplied model is glm(elo_avg ~ randomization*skills_count + msg_count, data=df), line 60. This check did not re-estimate the paper's conflicting Elo p-values.

elo_real_vs_simulated.csv supplies 431 individual campaign records: basegpt=116, creativegpt=114, creativegpt_rand=101, sim=100. Columns are randomization, creativity, themes_num, llm_rating, elo_rating; all are populated. It covers S1-O3 and the S2 benchmark but contains no participant/campaign identifier, so arm summaries are possible without a person-level merge; do not assume row order identifies participants. creativity is an empirical percentile on a 0-1 scale in this file. Plotting code multiplies by 100. Among sim rows, 99 llm_rating values are 8 and one is 7, differing from the saved PDF's statement that all 100 scored 8. creativity_analysis.R drops sim campaigns scored 7 for its plot. The exact analysis sample and scale must be matched before reproducing printed main-text results.

has_texts_or_ideas=true has limited scope: all 331 participants have nonempty baseline DAT_1 through DAT_10 and AUT_1/AUT_2 text responses in the main data; these precede the experimental marketing task. simulated_campaigns.csv also has campaign_text for 250 simulated campaigns (125 per prompt condition), not the participants' experimental campaigns and not established as the exact 100-campaign S2 sample. The README explicitly says 'Raw participant messages and AI responses are excluded to protect participant privacy' and 'Campaign evaluation scores are provided without the underlying campaign text'. No participant marketing_answer/campaign_text, extracted participant campaign themes, campaign theme embeddings, or raw conversation files were found in the complete inventory. Classified message/response files have labels and participant IDs, not message text. Textual LLM evaluation rationales are present but are not a substitute for the underlying participant campaign texts. New diversity measures of the experimental campaign texts cannot be calculated from this release.

human_campaign_evaluations.csv has 331 participant-linked rows and elaboration, feasibility, novelty, overall, value scores. These IDs match the main dataset. Batch_5322742_batch_results.csv has 1655 rating rows and the same 331 participant IDs. These are not identified as the saved PDF's 100-campaign expert-human pairwise Elo validation (S1-O2). The two supplementary 100-row files have condition and campaign_id, with campaign_id unique only within condition (50 per condition), but neither has an Elo column or participant_id. Do not infer that their 50/50 split is the human Elo sample's arm split. The 100-campaign human Elo data were not identified.

Relevant code is public but cannot run unchanged from these exports: preprocessing.R references absent raw files 'CreativityBot Experiment - V2_March 25, 2025_16.47.csv' and 'CreativityBot_Experiment_randomprofile.csv'; creativity_analysis.R requires the removed marketing_answer column and absent data/simulation/personalized_campaigns_simulated.csv. It constructs a centroid across human and simulated campaigns, calculates 1 minus cosine similarity, and converts sorted values to a 0-100 percentile grid (lines 160-208). Its plot CIs are mean +/- 1.96 * SD/sqrt(n) (lines 240-247). sensitivity_elo_creativity.R instead uses ecdf(campaign_uniqueness) (line 188), giving a related but not identical percentile convention. The untransformed theme vectors and raw text are unavailable, so the posted scores cannot be regenerated or their centroid independently checked. The pre-exclusion allocation/exclusion logs are absent.

what_we_could_compute: S1-O1, S1-O4, S1-O5, S1-O6: compute arm-specific means, sample SDs, SEs of the means, and outcome-specific analyzed counts from campaign_quality_score, campaign_wc, total_campaign_components, and marketing_terms_wc in the 331-row participant dataset. All four outcomes are observed for 116 generic, 114 personalized, and 101 partially personalized participants.

S1-O1 LLM Elo robustness analysis: compute per-person means of run_1 through run_5, then arm means, SDs, SEs and counts; the IDs and assignments match the main dataset. The supplied model formula and skills_count/msg_count covariates permit re-estimating the disputed personalized Elo contrast in final.open_items. The exported-column indexing in the script needs correction; the exact 0.02-versus-0.03 discrepancy was not resolved in this availability check.

S1-O3 and S2-O1: compute arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed output counts, quality-stratum counts, and between-arm contrasts for the existing creativity percentile scores in the 431-row elo_real_vs_simulated.csv (multiply by 100 for the plotted scale). These are individual output scores, not aggregate summaries. Lack of participant IDs prevents a verified participant-level covariate merge. The included 100 AI-only outputs include one quality-7 campaign, so the paper's benchmark sample/filter must be reconciled before matching its results.

final.open_items on creativity transformation, confidence intervals, and centroid: posted code documents inverse cosine similarity, percentile conversion, inclusion of simulated campaigns in the combined pool, and plotted CIs of mean +/- 1.96*SD/sqrt(n). It therefore supplies material to clarify these methods, but the main and Elo scripts use different percentile conventions; missing participant text/theme embeddings prevent independent reconstruction of the underlying scores.

final.open_items on the AI-only coefficient: the public arm-labelled creativity scores permit fitting an explicit AI-only-versus-human-AI contrast, but do not on their own establish which reference/model produced the paper's beta=-21.9. A reproduced chosen model is not confirmation of the authors' unspecified model.

Not recoverable from this release: pre-exclusion allocation totals and exclusions by arm; new diversity measures from participant experimental campaign text; and S1-O2's 100-campaign expert-human Elo means, SDs, SEs, or arm counts. Baseline DAT/AUT texts are available but cannot estimate a treatment effect on the later marketing-campaign texts. Manuscript-version correspondence, exact deployed task-duration instructions, and the word-count codebook classification also remain outside what these data establish.
notes:
Availability checked on 2026-10-09. Read the complete 151997-character markdown conversion, including all appendices (saved PDF: 62 pages, main pp. 1-28 and supplement pp. 1-34). The statement quotations were verified with PyMuPDF text extraction; only whitespace/line wraps were normalized. The full PDF's embedded hyperlinks contain exactly two distinct repository URLs, both checked. Supplementary methods, prompts, and aggregate tables are appended to the saved PDF; they do not supply the participant rows themselves.

High confidence in public_participant_data because anonymous downloads directly confirmed participant_id, randomization, and multiple outcome columns in 331 unique participant rows. This status does not mean every requested measure is recoverable. Raw participant campaign text is withheld; only existing creativity scores can be summarized for the experimental outputs. The has_texts_or_ideas=true flag is specifically for baseline DAT/AUT responses and separate AI simulations, not the experimental human-AI campaign texts.

Two related public deposits were found: the code/data project and its registration. Searches identified no additional relevant deposit. OSF API listings, not the generic JavaScript landing-page shell, establish public file availability. No login, access request, author contact, or paid API was used; downloads stayed in memory and were all below 20 MB.

The data's categorical arm counts agree with the saved PDF (generic 116, personalized 114, partial 101). The currently hosted arXiv abstract reverses the two personalized labels/counts, so it was not used to map the dataset. The exact match between the saved undated manuscript and the later arXiv version remains unconfirmed. Repository code and several evaluation exports also require version/schema reconciliation before an exact numerical reproduction.

Registration history was inspected: the 2025-01-21 registration has an approved amendment submitted 2025-03-10 for the marketing task. The amendment describes two assistant conditions, not all three analyzed arms. This narrows the registration open item but does not establish prospective specification of the complete analyzed design or outcome hierarchy.
